correction.truth: They are carved Greek letters: the dedication.

c1b.text: Yes. This is the inscription: Cheramyes dedicated me to Hera as an offering.

correction.tempting: Pleats run down her body too.

correction.truth: Her toes are bare, resting on the round base.
correction.evidence: The crop; Girard (1880); the Louvre record.

correction.tempting: They are rounded and in a row.
correction.truth: They are her toes, on the round base.
correction.evidence: The crop; Girard (1880); the Louvre record.

c2c.text: Yes. Bare toes on a round base, carved from the same block as the statue.

c2m.text: Bare toes on a round base.

c3q.text: What crosses her chest on a slant?

c3a.text: Yes: the himation, slung across her right shoulder and chest, over a fine linen tunic.

correction.truth: The slanting folds are her cloak, the himation.
correction.evidence: The Louvre; the Samos museum book (2012).

correction.truth: The veil falls over her back and left leg; across the chest is the cloak.
correction.evidence: The Louvre; the Louvre record; the Samos museum book (2012).

correction.tempting: Old statues often lose their bases.
correction.truth: Her round base survives, carved in one piece with the statue.

c4b.text: Yes. With her head went part of her left shoulder and arm. Her twin is broken in the same places.

c4c.text: Her right arm is still there.

correction.tempting: Her arms are hard to make out under the cloth.
correction.truth: Her right arm runs down her side. The missing parts are on her left.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; Touchais (1985); the photo.

c4m.text: Headless and one-armed, like her twin.

extends.concept: From what the inscription says (level) to where it is carved: down the front edge of her veil

c1q.what_you_learn: Her dedication is carved in a single line of Greek letters down the front edge of her veil.
